Note 4 (ticket 1), written by Compliance agent:

Source Code is owned by Engineer, and Analyst does not own it, so admin is not permitted. As a full-time employee, maximum is write (policy 1). Requested level (admin) exceeds maximum, so grant the maximum: write.
Note 5 (ticket 1), written by Facilities agent:

reason: Five sources (HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities) confirm Alexandra Johnson (E003) is a full-time Analyst. content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee E003, Alexandra Johnson, requests admin access to Source Code.

Notes:
- HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities all say: full-time Analyst, maximum write (admin only if role owns system, Analyst doesn't own Source Code; Engineer owns it). Recommendation: write.
- Security agent says: contractor with basic security training, max read, recommendation read. This differs from other DBs.

So there's a discrepancy. Most agents say full-time Analyst; Security says contractor. 

As the Approver, I need to make the final decision. The policy: full-time employees up to write; contractor read or write if advanced training; never admin.

Regardless of whether she's full-time Analyst or contractor, admin is not permitted. The requested level is admin, which exceeds both potential maximums. So grant the maximum.

But what is the maximum? If full-time Analyst: write. If contractor basic training: read.

Most sources (5 agents) say full-time Analyst. Security says contractor. Hmm. Which to trust? The majority of DBs confirm full-time Analyst. But Security DB is a security-related check. The Security agent has a note that says it differs from other DBs.

As Approver, I should weigh the evidence. Five agents across different systems (HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities) confirm full-time Analyst. Security is one agent with contradicting info. The majority supports full-time Analyst.

Under policy for full-time employee: max is write (Analyst doesn't own Source Code). Requested admin exceeds max, so grant write.

Alternatively, if we take contractor: max read. But majority evidence supports full-time.

I'll go with write based on the preponderance of evidence. The final decision: write.

Let me submit with reason.
